extracted.intended_audience: public company management, investor relations professionals, and corporate counsel
extracted.subtask_short: Regulation FD compliance for public companies
extracted.subtask_description: Practical best-practices and compliance criteria for public companies on selective disclosure under Regulation FD — how to talk to investors, analysts and securities market professionals and how/when to publicly disclose material nonpublic information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designate spokespersons and control information flow
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorize a limited number of spokespersons – typically the CEO, CFO and the head of investor relations. All other employees should be instructed to refer all inquiries to these authorized spokespersons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Control information flow and ensure counsel and disclosure teams are involved in evaluating materiality and whether information has been previously publicly disclosed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adhere to a 'no comment' policy for rumors
rubrics_metrics.description: For rumors concerning material developments or pending transactions (including M&A), the standard response is that it is the company’s policy to not comment on such rumors or respond to such inquiries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid other responses (e.g., saying a rumor is baseless or 'not aware') because they are inconsistent with the policy and potentially problematic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implement protocol for conference calls and webcasts
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish formal protocols governing public calls and webcasts with investors and analysts to ensure broad, non-exclusionary distribution of information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protocol should address advance notice, scripts, opening safe-harbor statements, replay availability, and counsel review to avoid Regulation FD and other liabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximize advance notice and participation for conference calls
rubrics_metrics.description: Always allow broad participation in the conference call; provide advance public notice of call details (date, time, how to access) via press release and company website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide as much advance notice as possible (several days minimum for regular quarterly earnings calls); only hold the call after the press release is broadly disseminated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Always use a script for investor calls
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare a script for each call and have it reviewed by counsel for accuracy and completeness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counsel review helps avoid non-Regulation FD issues such as anti-fraud liability, unintentionally creating a duty to update, or 'gun-jumping' for offerings or transactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Always begin calls with the forward-looking safe harbor
rubrics_metrics.description: Invoke the forward-looking statement safe harbor at the start of every conference call.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulation FD does not change the need to rely on the safe harbor for forward-looking statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make audio replays available to the public for a limited time
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide audio replays of calls or webcasts through the company website for a limited period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A week or so is appropriate, especially if information is changing rapidly; indicate in notice how and for how long replay/transcript will be available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise extreme caution in one-on-one calls/meetings
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosures of material nonpublic information in one-on-one or limited access meetings are selective disclosure and can violate Regulation FD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minimize risk by holding meetings near earnings releases, avoiding blackout periods, setting ground rules about off-limit questions (projections, internal bases), and including an IR representative or debriefing with IR and counsel post-meeting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid commenting on earnings estimates and draft analyst reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not provide private 'guidance' to investors or analysts about earnings estimates, and do not review or comment on draft analyst reports except in very limited ways.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If commenting is necessary, do so only in a public conference call after an earnings release; if reviewing analyst drafts, limit comments to historical facts or business descriptions and state the limited scope and that you are not endorsing projections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary goal: create a level playing field
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulation FD's purpose is to create a level playing field for all investors with respect to a company's material nonpublic information by prohibiting selective disclosures to certain persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When material nonpublic information is disclosed to covered persons, the company must publicly disclose that information promptly (for unintentional) or simultaneously (for intentional).

rubrics_metrics.name: Companies subject to Regulation FD
rubrics_metrics.description: U.S. public companies (issuers with securities registered under Section 12 or required to file under Section 15(d)), other than foreign private issuers, are subject to Regulation FD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stock exchange rules may impose similar timely disclosure obligations on foreign private issuers (FPIs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Company representatives covered by Regulation FD
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulation FD applies to 'senior officials' and persons who regularly communicate with investors/analysts, including directors, executive officers, investor relations/public relations personnel, and other employees/agents who regularly communicate with market professionals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Others are not subject unless directed to disclose by a senior official; a director appointed by an investor is considered a senior official and subject to the rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients covered by Regulation FD
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule applies when material nonpublic information is disclosed to brokers/dealers, investment advisers, institutional investment managers, investment companies (and persons associated with them), or holders when it is reasonably foreseeable they will trade on the information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclusions include disclosures to persons owing a duty of trust/confidence (e.g., bankers, accountants), persons who expressly agree to maintain confidentiality, and disclosures in connection with most registered securities offerings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Materiality standard: traditional materiality analysis applies
rubrics_metrics.description: Materiality is judged by whether a reasonable investor would consider the information important to an investment decision or whether it would significantly alter the total mix of information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical materially categories include earnings (incl. guidance), M&A, new product announcements, changes in control, management changes, auditor changes, securities events (dividends, splits, defaults), cybersecurity incidents, and bankruptcy. SAB No. 99 emphasizes no bright-line quantitative tests—facts and circumstances control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mosaic theory: aggregating immaterial items
rubrics_metrics.description: An immaterial item disclosed to an analyst that is combined with other information to form a material 'mosaic' is not itself a Regulation FD violation under SEC guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus of materiality is the reasonable investor, not the recipient; SEC has said immaterial disclosures that contribute to a mosaic are not per se violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard of review for violations: knowing or reckless
rubrics_metrics.description: To violate Regulation FD, the person making the disclosure must know, or be reckless in not knowing, that the information disclosed is both material and nonpublic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a relatively high standard and provides a safeguard for companies acting in good faith; repeated errors, however, can increase risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonpublic information: general rule — widely available = public
rubrics_metrics.description: Information is 'public' if disseminated in a manner that makes it widely available to investors and typically available for a reasonable period for the market to digest it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information from someone other than the company or unnamed media sources is unlikely to be 'public' for Reg FD purposes; the time requirement does not apply if disseminated by Form 8-K.

rubrics_metrics.name: Website disclosure criteria (recognized channel, accessibility, waiting period)
rubrics_metrics.description: Three considerations govern whether website-posted information is public: (1) is the company's website a recognized channel of distribution; (2) is the information posted in a manner that is readily accessible to investors and the markets; (3) has there been a reasonable waiting period for the market to digest the information?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factors for recognized channel include: notifying the market of the website, consistent practice of posting important information, website design leading investors to important info, degree of market/media access and redistribution, use of push technology (RSS), and whether the site is kept current and accurate. Reasonable waiting period depends on company size/following and information complexity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social media: apply website guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: The SEC's social media guidance says the same website factors apply to social media channels when evaluating recognized channels of distribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Companies must evaluate whether the social media used is a recognized channel of distribution using the same factors used for websites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manner of dissemination — methods that satisfy public disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Public disclosure can be made by furnishing or filing a Form 8-K, issuing a press release through widely circulated news/wire services, or by other methods reasonably designed to provide broad non-exclusionary distribution (press conferences, conference calls, webcasts) provided the public has adequate notice and means to access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other Exchange Act documents (Form 10-Q, proxy) can satisfy the requirement if the disclosure is timely, conspicuous, not buried, and not piecemeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of required disclosure: intentional vs non-intentional
rubrics_metrics.description: If the selective disclosure was intentional, the company must disclose the same information to the public simultaneously; if non-intentional, the company must disclose the same information promptly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intent is a facts-and-circumstances test; 'simultaneous' generally means at or before the time of the intentional disclosure; 'promptly' is defined more specifically (see Promptly entry).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'Intentional' selective disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: An intentional selective disclosure occurs when the person making the disclosure either knows, or is reckless in not knowing, that the information communicated is both material and nonpublic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if the speaker had not planned to disclose the information, if they knew it was material and nonpublic and provided it, the disclosure is intentional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'Promptly' for non-intentional disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Promptly' means as soon as reasonably practicable but in no event after the later of 24 hours or the commencement of the next trading day on the NYSE after a senior official learns (or is reckless in not knowing) that a non-intentional disclosure of material nonpublic information occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quick materiality determinations are often needed when answering unanticipated questions; have a disclosure team including counsel on call to evaluate and respond rapidly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulation FD and securities offerings
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulation FD generally does not apply to disclosures in registered securities offerings (with limited exceptions), and does not apply to traditional road shows in registered offerings; it does apply to unregistered offerings and to communications before and after registered offerings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For unregistered offerings, obtain confidentiality agreements from investors or publicly disclose material nonpublic information; certain shelf offerings have special treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confirmations of prior forecasts can be material
rubrics_metrics.description: A confirmation of an issuer's own prior forecast may be material if it conveys additional information beyond the original forecast or if timing/intervening events make the confirmation informative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example considerations include time elapsed since original forecast, intervening events (e.g., a major customer ceasing operations). Saying 'not changed' or 'still comfortable' can be equivalent to confirming and treated as material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulation FD does not create a duty to update
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulation FD does not change existing law regarding any duty to update previously disclosed information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate legal doctrines govern duties to update; Reg FD itself does not impose a new duty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewing analyst models: permissible if no material nonpublic info communicated
rubrics_metrics.description: An issuer may review or comment on an analyst's model privately if it does not communicate material nonpublic information — e.g., correcting historical facts or sharing inconsequential data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use model discussions as a vehicle (explicitly or implicitly) to convey material nonpublic information; be cautious about implying confirmation of forecasts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality agreements: express agreement to maintain confidentiality is required for exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: To rely on Regulation FD's exclusion, the recipient must expressly agree to maintain the information in confidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No additional promise not to trade is required for the exclusion; merely acknowledging receipt or agreeing not to trade is not sufficient—must be an express confidentiality agreement; trading by the recipient still could lead to insider trading liability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Road shows: registered-offering road shows excluded; others are covered
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosures made 'in connection with' a registered public offering of the type excluded from Regulation FD (including road shows) are not subject to Regulation FD; disclosures in road shows for unregistered offerings are subject to Regulation FD unless a confidentiality agreement is in place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mini-road shows during private placements are covered by Reg FD even if a resale registration is later filed; obtain confidences or publicly disclose material info where required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communications to employees are not Reg FD disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulation FD applies to disclosures made to persons outside the issuer; communications to employees (even if they are shareholders) do not trigger Reg FD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employees remain subject to duties of trust and insider-trading rules; exercise caution and consider confidentiality obligations internally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unauthorized senior-official disclosures may be breaches of duty (not covered by Reg FD)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a senior official not authorized under company policy makes selective disclosures, those disclosures are breaches of trust/confidence and are not covered by Regulation FD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such breaches may nonetheless trigger insider trading liability or other consequences—implement pre-clearance and speaker-authority policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Private shareholder meetings are not adequate public disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: A shareholder meeting that is open to the public but not webcast/broadcast or otherwise reasonably designed for broad distribution is not sufficient to satisfy Regulation FD public-disclosure requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presence of press at an otherwise non-public meeting does not by itself render the meeting public for Reg FD purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conference call notice requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Adequate advance notice for a conference call under Regulation FD must include date, time, subject matter and call-in information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider timing (reasonable period ahead; several days for regular quarterly calls), and indicate whether transcripts or replays will be available and for how long.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exchange Act filings other than Form 8-K can constitute public disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: A Form 10-Q, proxy statement or other publicly filed EDGAR document can satisfy Reg FD public disclosure if information is timely, conspicuous, not buried, and not disclosed piecemeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bring the disclosure to readers' attention within the filing; confirm the filing is accepted and publicly available on EDGAR before relying on it as public disclosure prior to a private discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure EDGAR acceptance before relying on a filing as public
rubrics_metrics.description: Before making private disclosures that rely on a filing as public disclosure, the issuer should confirm the filing or furnishing has been accepted and is publicly available on EDGAR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This avoids premature private disclosure before the information is available to the public.
